items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1978-12-03
items.q: I played, actually, ordered a clarinet from Charlie Parker in Houston, the band director that came out in the barns park

ctx.x: They did play well. Do you remember the names of any of them?

Well, the country fiddler was my Uncle Gus Clayton. And he was a Mississippi and played four dances out in the country, you know, just like those square dances and things like that. My father was often worried. He'd say, there you go. You're going to be like Uncle Gus, playing that music. They were not particularly interested in having me play, but my sisters were all far and my mother died when I was very young. And I became interested in playing. We had a school, East End School band in Marshall. And I had been…
Did you have, could you play by ear or were you?
